[Thinking]
**Calculating average distance in astronomy**

The user asked a straightforward factual question, so I'll provide the average distance and variability related to astronomical units. One astronomical unit is approximately 149.6 million km, with perihelion at about 147.1 million km and aphelion around 152.1 million km. In miles, that's about 93 million miles. Also, light takes roughly 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel this distance. I’ll keep the answer concise and clear!
[/Thinking]

- Average distance (1 Astronomical Unit): about 149.6 million km (93 million miles)
- Varies from ~147.1 million km at perihelion to ~152.1 million km at aphelion
- Light travel time: about 8 minutes 20 seconds
